presentation.title: Drug Interaction Data Engineering & Analysis
presentation.subtitle: An end-to-end pipeline that turns the official Spanish CIMA dataset into a structured, NLP-enriched and queryable resource — and uses it to compare two NoSQL databases for managing drug-interaction data.

etl.title: A complete, verified ETL pipeline
etl.takeaway: The source XML is reconciled against both databases with zero referential-integrity violations — the data is complete and consistent.

nlp.title: From free text to structured clinical attributes
nlp.evaluatedOn: Evaluated on all {{count}} distinct interaction texts (a census of the corpus). Severity is near-perfect for both; spaCy generalises better on type. Mechanism is rarely stated in the source text.
nlp.takeaway: Two NLP approaches turn Spanish free text into queryable severity, type and mechanism — applied to 100% of the {{total}} interactions.

graph.title: Interaction network of one drug (graph view)
graph.subtitle: {{count}} interactions for {{drug}}
graph.takeaway: One drug can interact with dozens of others — exactly the connected structure a graph database is built to traverse.

lookup.title: Live drug-interaction lookup
lookup.hint: Search the official CIMA catalogue and see a medicine's real interactions, ranked by severity.
lookup.placeholder: Type a medicine name… e.g. Sintrom
lookup.noInteractions: No interactions recorded for this medicine.
lookup.takeaway: A clinician could type any medicine and instantly see its documented interactions ranked by severity — the project's data made directly useful.

db.title: A fair, measured database comparison
db.scalabilityTitle: Scalability — latency growth from 25% → 100% data (lower scales better)
db.takeaway: No single winner: Neo4j dominates aggregation, traversal and multi-hop queries (and scales better), while MongoDB wins simple indexed lookups — the optimal store depends on the workload.

closing.title: In one sentence
closing.text: A reproducible system that engineers, enriches and compares the official Spanish drug-interaction data — answering all three research questions with measured results and a working, explorable application.
